newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks seen making further gains.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks seen making further gains.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks, which closed at a 26-month high on Tuesday, are expected to make further gains when trading resumes, brokers saidy.
"There is enough local and foreign buying to sustain an upward movement depsite a little profit-taking," said Aslem Ahmed of CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch Stock Brokers.
Heavy buying pushed the all share index over 800 points on Tuesday, to close at 804.2 points, on turnover of 346.8 million rupees.
Brokers said foreigners were buying pricey blue chips while local investors were searching out the lower valued counters.
"The buying pattern reflects anticipated economic growth," said Manjula Kumarasinghe of brokerage Jardine Fleming HNB.
"There is a lot of buying interest in stocks like Lanka Lubricants, plantation shares, conglomerates, manufacturing and hotel sectors," he added.
Brokers said many shares were not over-valued at current levels.
"While manufacturing and hotel shares are still under-valued, conglomerates are fast reaching full valuations," said Ahmed of CDIC Sasoon.
